newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe concedes defeat in French election.
newsitem.headline: Juppe concedes defeat in French election.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe conceded defeat for his centre-right coalition in a parliamentary election runoff on Sunday and wished the left-wing opposition well in government.

"We did not manage to convince the French people that we were going in the right direction," Juppe said in a brief statement in his Bordeaux constituency after computer projections showed the non-communist left heading for an absolute majority of National Assembly seats.
"The people have spoken. Their decision is sovereign. We all respect it. I wish good luck to those who will now govern France and I wish good luck to France," the outgoing premier said.
Juppe announced last Monday he would resign whatever the outcome of Sunday's decisive runoff following the centre-right's disastrous performance in the first round on May 25.

He was widely blamed by conservative colleagues and the left-wing opposition for two years of austerity, record 12.8 percent unemployment and higher taxes to qualify France for a single European currency, which led to the election defeat.
